subject: Entity mapping, SWIFT copy format, and fee-absorption for international collections
messages:
From: Andrew Holt <andrew.holt@acme-corp.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: finops@acme-consulting.com
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Entity mapping + SWIFT copy format + intermediary fee approach

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this — we're finalizing the payment rails for our upcoming integration and need a few clarifications from Redwood finance to avoid reconciliation friction: 

1) Entity mapping: we have 3 paying entities (Acme US, Acme UK, Acme EU). Can you confirm which Redwood collection entity/account each invoice should point to so our AP team can automate remittance? I've attached the Acme entity matrix.

2) SWIFT copy / MT103: our treasury team requires a beneficiary account + full chain of intermediaries on the remittance advice for automatic matching. What SWIFT copy format does Redwood produce and which fields should we expect for multi-hop wires? A short example would help.

3) Intermediary bank fees: for multi-hop rails, who absorbs the intermediary/correspondent fees? We prefer to net (beneficiary receives amount minus intermediary fees) but need to know if Redwood can accept net receipts or if you require sender-cover (OUR).

4) VAT / invoice treatment: for cross-border settlement, please confirm whether Redwood issues VAT-included or VAT-exempt invoices for EU customers and which VAT ID we should include on the remittance.

Can you respond with the collection account mapping, a sample SWIFT copy, and your default stance on fee absorbing vs OUR? If there's flexibility, outline options and any additional charges.

Appreciate it — aim is to have this locked before our finance cutover on July 1.

Best,
Andrew
Treasury Manager | Acme Corp
(Attachment: acme_entity_matrix.xlsx)

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Holt <andrew.holt@acme-corp.com>
Cc: finops@acme-consulting.com, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Entity mapping + SWIFT copy format + intermediary fee approach

Hi Andrew,

Thanks — this is helpful. Quick answers below and a proposed mapping. Attaching our collection guidance and a sample SWIFT copy for a three-hop wire.

Proposed entity mapping (please confirm):
- Invoices for Acme US -> Pay to: Redwood Inc (US collections) — account ending ...4321 (USD)
- Invoices for Acme UK -> Pay to: Redwood EMEA Ltd (UK collections) — account ending ...2210 (GBP)
- Invoices for Acme EU -> Pay to: Redwood Europe B.V. (NL EUR collections) — account ending ...1187 (EUR)

SWIFT copy: attached sample_swift_copy.txt — we include: sending bank BIC, sender account, full intermediary chain (if present), beneficiary BIC/account, remittance narrative (invoice refs). Our clearing partner provides MT103-like text in the remittance file.

Intermediary fees: our default is to accept net receipts (BEN) for standard SaaS collections to avoid payout retries. That means beneficiary receives amount net of intermediary fees. If Acme requires OUR, we can accept but it requires sender-side instruction and may trigger reconciliation differences — and sometimes intermediary banks still deduct unexpectedly.

VAT: Redwood issues invoices according to the billing entity: Redwood EMEA Ltd invoices will include VAT where applicable (we will include Redwood VAT ID on the invoice). For Acme UK/EU customers we recommend providing the paying entity's VAT ID on the remittance so our AR team can apply the correct tax treatment.

If acceptable, I'll loop in Marissa from Revenue Ops to confirm the acceptance of net receipts for the Acme account and Laura from Legal for anything that needs contract-side language (e.g., fee responsibility).

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood_collection_guidelines.pdf; Attachment: sample_swift_copy.txt)

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, Andrew Holt <andrew.holt@acme-corp.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 20 Jun 2028 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Entity mapping + SWIFT copy format + intermediary fee approach

Hi all —

Looping in our Payments team notes and one operational caveat: we can default to BENEFICIARY-PAID (net) for Acme collections. Operational details: 
- When net is chosen, our AR will match incoming MT103 text to invoice refs; please ensure the invoice references are present in the beneficiary narrative.
- For large monthly remittances where Acme wants a gross amount, we can accept OUR instructions, but we will reconcile any differences and bill any unexpected correspondent charges back to Acme on the next invoice. 

Sample SWIFT snippet (from attached sample_swift_copy.txt):
---
23B: CRED
32A: 220618EUR12345,00
50K: /ACMEUS/12345678
53A: BANKUS33
56A: CORRUS33
57A: REDWNL22
59: /NL12REDW0000001187
70: INV 2028-07-01 / ACME-PO-9876
---

Please confirm which mode you prefer (NET/BEN vs OUR) for July collections and whether your team can include PO/invoice refs on the payment instruction.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Revenue Ops — Payments
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: payments_processing_notes.txt)

From: Andrew Holt <andrew.holt@acme-corp.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: finops@acme-consulting.com
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Entity mapping + SWIFT copy format + intermediary fee approach

Thanks Marissa — that SWIFT example is exactly what we needed.

Acme preference for July 1 cutover: NET (BEN) for standard monthly invoices. We'll add the invoice references in the payment narrative. For one-off high-value transfers we will send OUR and notify Redwood treasury ahead of time; please confirm Redwood will invoice any unexpected correspondent charges back to us in the following monthly bill if OUR still results in deductions.

Also: can you confirm the exact VAT ID string to include for Redwood EMEA Ltd on remittances? We need it in our AP system.

Best,
Andrew
Treasury Manager | Acme Corp

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Holt <andrew.holt@acme-corp.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Entity mapping + SWIFT copy format + intermediary fee approach

Hi Andrew —

Confirmed items from Redwood legal/finance: 
- VAT ID for Redwood EMEA Ltd: NL999999999B01 (please include exactly as shown on remittances).
- Net (BEN) receipts are acceptable as Redwood's default for recurring SaaS collections. For OUR payments, we will perform normal reconciliation and will include any non-standard correspondent charges back to Acme on the subsequent invoice (with supporting SWIFT/MT103 evidence).
- We'll update the MSA addendum to explicitly state that intermediary/correspondent fees are the responsibility of the payer unless a separate written agreement is in place to absorb them. If you want Redwood to absorb fees for a specific invoice, please include that instruction in the purchase order and notify kimberly.park@redwood.ai in advance so Accounts can route reconciliation.

Next steps: Kimberly — please confirm the final mapping in your system and we'll send a short one-page addendum reflecting the fee policy for signature. Andrew — if you can confirm NET/BEN for the recurring July payment and attach a sample payment instruction from your bank, we'll validate the mapping and test-match on a small EUR test transfer next week.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Finance & Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: fee_policy_addendum_draft.pdf)
